source.title: Feature: BS-18 — Governed two-principal access-control assessment in BeeScan Web
source.body:
### Summary

Extend the existing BeeScan Web investigation runtime with bounded, independently authenticated read-only access-control comparisons, including safe principal isolation, evidence authentication and end-to-end Finding review/report integration.

### Type

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Chore
- [ ] Idea

### Roadmap / iteration

- Iteration: **BS-18 — Governed Multi-Principal Access Control Assessment MVP**
- Stage: **10 — Verification, Operator Workspace and Challenge Readiness**
- Goal from `docs/product/beescan_roadmap.md`: Execute governed comparative access-control assessments using independently authorized test principals and provide authenticated evidence to BeeScan It18.

### Context

BeeAgent v0.90.0 already implements:

- Authenticated BeeScan Web Investigation.
- Dynamic target policy for authorized public HTTP(S) origins.
- Governed discovery and DAST execution.
- Managed egress with DNS/IP/TLS binding and cleanup.
- Request and deadline accounting.
- ArtifactAPI, signed Case ownership and Web receipts.
- Protected Human Review, Report and Export.

Verified gaps:

- The Web Start contract has no target test-principal selection.
- Existing DAST mediation does not provide independent authenticated upstream sessions.
- Existing review source restoration is DAST-specific.
- No host-owned principal/object authorization matrix exists for comparative read-only assessment.

Web Console operator identities are not target application test identities.

Companion: BeeScan It18.

Completed prerequisites: BeeScan It17 and BeeAgent BS-17.

### Scope

**Included**

- Define a minimal, fail-closed, host-owned two-principal test profile.
- Support exactly two explicitly authorized test identities for the initial profile.
- Bind the profile to exact approved origin, operator, Case, validity, scope, permitted GET resources and request budget.
- Reference session credentials through approved environment-backed secret sources; never persist their values in ordinary configuration or artifacts.
- Validate that principal contexts are independently bound to test-account identity using approved identity observations.
- Provide a minimal protected profile-selection mechanism in the existing Web Workspace.
- Obtain approved observed resource references through existing discovery or a separately authenticated source observation.
- Execute bounded GET-only owner and cross-principal requests through existing governed HTTP/network infrastructure.
- Apply one immutable test-principal context to each request; prohibit accidental fallback or context inheritance.
- Preserve existing DNS/IP/TLS restrictions, exact origin, redirect refusal, deadlines, egress lifecycle and cleanup.
- Normalize bounded private-object proof into non-sensitive authenticated evidence.
- Preserve exact Case, principal, resource, request, response, source and provider provenance.
- Delegate authorization-violation evaluation to BeeScan It18.
- Extend the existing Case/Results, Human Review, Report and Export workflow for access-control Findings.
- Preserve safe terminal statuses, exact request accounting, restart persistence and evidence read-back.
- Maintain existing Path Traversal, CLI, Web Investigation, legacy Case and DAST behavior.

**Excluded**

- Login automation, password guessing and arbitrary identity creation.
- General-purpose secret management or credential vault development.
- Arbitrary Cookies/Authorization headers supplied to a scanner or AI.
- Cross-origin authenticated requests.
- Unapproved object identifiers, unrestricted enumeration or broad crawling.
- POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE or GET operations known to mutate state.
- ZAP Access Control add-on integration in this MVP.
- Generic browser automation and second execution/runtime engines.
- Unsupervised VERIFIED, bounty submission or privilege-changing exploitation.
- BeeUI and BeeSDK changes without separately approved blockers.
- Cosmetic Web Workspace redesign.

### Deliverable

`Target + Task + Approved Two-Principal Profile → Authenticated Discovery/Source → Governed Comparative GET → BeeScan Access-Control Result → Finding / PARTIAL → Review → Report → Export`

The ordinary Web Workspace must complete the supported workflow.

### Acceptance Criteria

**Authority and principal isolation**

- [ ] Only authenticated and authorized BeeScan operators can select and execute approved test profiles.
- [ ] Two test identities are independently authenticated and distinguishable.
- [ ] Test credentials are scoped to one exact approved origin.
- [ ] Credentials cannot be attached to arbitrary Target URLs, redirects, DNS-rebound destinations or unrelated Cases.
- [ ] Missing, expired, revoked, mismatched or duplicate principal contexts fail closed.
- [ ] Principal IDs and approved roles are host-derived, not accepted as arbitrary execution authority from Web input.
- [ ] No secrets are passed to BeeScan, AI, ordinary artifacts, report previews or logs.
- [ ] Unsupported credential types and malformed authorization metadata are refused before target execution.

**Execution**

- [ ] The host selects an observed eligible read-only resource or accepts a separately authenticated approved source observation.
- [ ] A bounded owner baseline and cross-principal comparison execute with exact per-request principal binding.
- [ ] At least one horizontal and one vertical test scenario complete using the same reusable execution contract.
- [ ] No arbitrary object-ID generation or target-specific execution code is used.
- [ ] Requests use GET only; endpoints known to mutate state remain excluded.
- [ ] Redirects cannot transfer credentials or expand approved scope.
- [ ] DNS/IP/TLS binding, request budget, timeout, cancellation and verified cleanup work for both contexts.
- [ ] Request accounting includes attempted/partial requests and remains truthful after timeout or failure.
- [ ] Missing or invalid object-specific proof cannot create CANDIDATE.
- [ ] Fixed, intentionally public and ambiguous targets do not generate false-positive Findings.

**Web, review and persistence**

- [ ] The operator starts a new Case through the ordinary BeeScan Web Workspace.
- [ ] Supported access-control Findings appear in Results with authenticated evidence references.
- [ ] PARTIAL, REFUSED, ERROR and NO_MATCH remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Existing independent Review and Report actions support the new Finding family.
- [ ] JSON/Markdown preview and download use existing protected routes and source authentication.
- [ ] Foreign operators cannot access another operator's credentials, Case, Finding, review or report.
- [ ] Restart preserves completed Case and report integrity without persisting plaintext credentials.
- [ ] Active Resume requires renewed valid test-principal authority and cannot silently replay expired sessions.
- [ ] Review/Report/Export generate zero additional target requests.
- [ ] Existing Path Traversal Web E2E continues working.

**External acceptance**

- [ ] A controlled two-account vulnerable fixture produces a genuine evidence-backed horizontal CANDIDATE.
- [ ] A controlled privileged/non-privileged fixture produces a genuine evidence-backed vertical CANDIDATE.
- [ ] Corresponding fixed, public and ambiguous fixtures are handled correctly.
- [ ] A real authorized two-account benchmark is exercised through the ordinary Web UI.
- [ ] The selected external scenario and permission model are recorded before implementation; no one-account lab is claimed as multi-principal proof.
- [ ] The existing ROADMAP PortSwigger acceptance requirement is explicitly reconciled with actual supported read-only testing before closure.

### Change level

- [ ] low-risk
- [ ] runtime-risk
- [x] security-sensitive

### Config / Contract impact

- [ ] no config or contract change expected
- [x] `config/settings.yml` may change
- [x] new required keys must be validated fail-fast
- [ ] module contract may change
- [x] artifact contract may change
- [x] capability / integration contract may change
- [x] CLI/runtime/transport behavior may change
- [x] docs update likely required

Expected owners:

- `integrations/beescan/policy.py` and existing authorization boundaries.
- Existing `http_runner.py`, managed egress and mediation mechanisms.
- `integrations/beescan/investigation.py` and `web.py`.
- Existing Case/ArtifactAPI and signed receipt handling.
- `integrations/beescan/review_source.py` and `review.py`.
- Existing `interfaces/ui/beescan.py` and BeeUI-backed action transport.
- BeeAgent `config/settings.yml` and corresponding fail-fast validation.
- `docs/WEB_UI.md` and applicable implementation contract documentation.

Exact changed files must be justified against the approved profile and existing implementation; do not introduce unrelated files or frameworks.

### Tests

**Automated**

- [x] unit/integration tests
- [x] `pytest -q`

**Smoke / runtime**

- [x] smoke checks through expected entrypoint
- [x] log verification
- [x] artifact verification

**Quality / security**

- [x] SAST
- [ ] SCA
- [x] DAST
- [ ] IAST
- [x] fuzzing
- [x] some checks are not applicable

Required automated coverage:

- Distinct authorized test identities.
- Same principal/session reused under two labels.
- Missing/expired/rotated credentials.
- Principal substitution and cross-Case replay.
- Wrong Target/origin and changed DNS resolution.
- Cross-origin redirects, unsupported methods and malformed URLs.
- Public, fixed, ambiguous and incomplete object access.
- Login-page HTTP 200 instead of object disclosure.
- Request budget exhaustion, timeout, cancellation and cleanup failure.
- Malformed evidence, substituted response digest and tampered ownership binding.
- Storage interruption, restart/read-back and signed receipt failure.
- Review evidence independence and report export ownership.
- Zero target traffic during Review/Report/Export.
- Legacy Path Traversal, DAST, Case and Web Workspace regressions.

Required runtime acceptance:

1. Start authorized test environment with two independently controlled principals.
2. Provision the approved credential and ownership profile.
3. Start a new assessment using the ordinary Web UI.
4. Inspect request accounting, execution lifecycle and authenticated evidence.
5. Confirm a genuine access-control CANDIDATE.
6. Perform independent Human Review.
7. Prepare and download a vulnerability report.
8. Restart and verify persisted Case/report integrity.
9. Repeat with fixed, public and ambiguous scenarios.
10. Confirm no secrets in ordinary logs, artifacts, JSON or HTML.
11. Run the full BeeAgent test suite and relevant paired BeeScan tests.
12. Record hosted CI and independent BeeMCP review results.

SCA applies if dependencies or pinned providers change. IAST is not required without an applicable instrumented runtime.

### Artifacts

Required bounded, authenticated outputs:

- Test-profile identity and authority reference without credentials.
- Per-principal request/evidence bindings.
- Comparative assessment result.
- Complete and truthful request/cleanup records.
- Existing Case and Web ownership receipts.
- Existing protected Finding review records.
- Existing vulnerability JSON/Markdown/report download outputs.

Use the current ArtifactAPI and protected storage.

Do not persist raw session cookies, Authorization headers, unrestricted response bodies or plaintext object secrets in ordinary artifacts.

### Security notes

- External connector involved: existing governed HTTP execution; no new third-party scanner.
- Email / attachment input involved: no.
- File/path handling involved: signed Case and evidence artifacts, protected export.
- Dependency changes involved: none planned.
- Serialization/parsing involved: strict test-profile, principal, source and result validation.
- Module / capability boundary involved: BeeAgent alone authorizes and executes requests; BeeScan performs offline evaluation.

Critical constraints:

- Web operator authentication and target test-principal authentication are separate trust boundaries.
- Every credential attachment requires exact-origin validation at execution time.
- The host must not rely on the domain result as network-execution permission.
- A successful HTTP response is not independent evidence of an authorization vulnerability.
- All release-blocking principal-isolation and confidentiality defects must be corrected in the same feature branch.

### Definition of Done

- [ ] behavior is implemented within the declared scope
- [ ] expected entrypoint/runtime behavior works
- [ ] tests are green
- [ ] logs are understandable
- [ ] artifacts are created/updated and consistent if applicable
- [ ] no secrets leak into logs/artifacts
- [ ] checks required for this task by `docs/SDLC.md` / `docs/SECURITY.md` are completed
- [ ] docs are updated if contract/behavior/artifacts changed
- [ ] result is ready to be closed through PR

Additional joint gate:

- BeeAgent uses the exact approved BeeScan It18 implementation.
- Genuine positive and negative multi-principal scenarios pass via ordinary Web UI.
- At least one representative real authorized benchmark is evidenced.
- PortSwigger requirement is reconciled without misrepresenting unsupported or state-changing tests.
- Finished Case, independent review and report survive restart.
- Existing Path Traversal and related Web workflows pass regression.
- Independent BeeMCP final review and hosted CI complete.
- **version not changed**

### Notes

- Coordinate implementation with BeeScan It18.
- Do not create a second HTTP runtime, generic secret manager or new scanner framework.
- Do not use Web Console principal IDs as target application identities.
- A test profile must be provisioned and validated before authenticated target execution.
- Use an editable sibling BeeScan dependency only for approved local implementation.
- Git-based BeeScan dependency handoff occurs through the agreed release process.
- Do not create BeeUI or BeeSDK branches.
- Do not modify unrelated ROADMAP, AGENTS, SECURITY or SDLC files.
- Use one coherent feature branch and one PR after explicit authorization.
